title: fix(app-shell): the bell's and Home's activity feed reads the app objects only (#12530)
body:
Fixes #12530
Clause-②: no

## What changed

The bell's Activity tab, the `global:notifications` bell and the console home's activity card all read one shared feed, `useSharedActivityFeed` in `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/sharedUserFeeds.ts`. That feed read `find('sys_activity', top 20, -timestamp)` with no object filter. Now:

1. **Roster-derived filter, in the query.** `activityObjectRoster(apps, gates)` collects every `type: 'object'` navigation entry's `objectName` across `filterActiveApps(apps)` (the launcher's own "an app the user can open" predicate), walking `areas[].navigation` and `navigation` at every group depth, each tree read through `navEntriesShownToMember` with the sidebar's own `useNavMemberGates` (object-read prune, `visible`, `requiredPermissions`, runtime capability). No object name and no `sys_` prefix is written anywhere. The read is `$filter: { object_name: { $in: roster } }` beside `$top: 20`, so the server caps business rows.
2. **The roster is part of the feed key** (`adapter:user:roster`). `SharedFeed.attach` drops the cached value and refetches on a new key (measured: a different `key` publishes `idle` and re-reads), so a roster that changes re-reads under the new filter.
3. **Never an unfiltered read.** The key stays null until the `app` metadata type is settled (`metadataTypeSettled(getTypeStatus('app'))`), so nothing is asked in that window. An empty roster answers `ready` with an empty feed and sends no request.
4. **Sign-in stamp excluded.** `isLoginStampRow` drops an `updated` row on `sys_user` whose `metadata.new` (the writer's diff) names only `last_login_at` / `last_login_ip`. That is the shape objectstack's `AuthManager.stampLastLogin` produces through plugin-audit's CRUD mirror. A `sys_user` edit that changes anything else is kept or dropped by the roster alone. This is the only post-read cut: the columns a query can name (`object_name`, `record_id`, `actor_id`, `type`) cannot tell a sign-in from a profile edit, and `metadata` is a JSON text column the server redacts per reader. So it can only shorten a page on a roster that lists `sys_user` (an admin's Setup app).
5. **Setup / audit unchanged.** The Setup surfaces read `sys_activity` through the generic object view and `RecordDetailView`, which this diff does not touch. Their suites (`views/RecordDetailView*`, `views/record-preview/`) ran green unchanged in the run below.

`layout/ActivityFeed.tsx` and `hooks/useHomeInbox.ts` needed no change: the filter lives in the one shared reading they both consume.

## Readings

- Login row shape (A2), read in objectstack `e4ec6ec1`. `stampLastLogin` issues `engine.update('sys_user', { id, last_login_at, last_login_ip? })`. plugin-audit's writer composes `type: activityTypeFor('update')` = `'updated'`, `object_name: ctx.object`, and `metadata: safeStringify({ old, new, ... })`, where `new` is `diff(before, after).next` with `updated_at` / `updated_by` dropped as noise.
- Setup's navigation (objectstack `platform-objects` `setup-nav.contributions.ts`) lists `sys_user`, `sys_organization`, `sys_team` and others, so an admin's roster legitimately contains those. No app lists `sys_jwks_key` or `sys_data_migration`. The `account` app lists `sys_*` objects but is `hidden: true`, so `filterActiveApps` skips it.
- A1: `SharedFeed` keys by a plain string. `attach` with a new key resets state and refetches, and `useSharedFeed`'s attach effect depends on `[feed, key]` only. The roster joins the key as a string (AGENTS.md #10: no memo identity is load-bearing).

## Tests (head `84b8f5632`)

- New pin `hooks/__tests__/sharedUserFeeds.activityRoster-12530.test.tsx`. Its fake adapter answers `$in` the way the server does, over the measured rows (JWKS key, data migration, owner backfill, sign-in stamp, a user edit, lead, account):
  - a roster of two app objects: the filter is exactly `{ object_name: { $in: ['crm_account', 'crm_lead'] } }` with `$top: 20`; no `sys_*` item is mapped; CONTROL: lead and account show;
  - hidden and inactive apps lend nothing, and an object the member may not read lends nothing;
  - with `sys_user` on the roster, the sign-in stamp is excluded; CONTROL: the user edit shows;
  - `isLoginStampRow` table;
  - app list loading: no read, `idle`; empty roster: no read, `ready`, empty;
  - a roster change re-reads under the new filter.
- Existing pins mount a roster now (shared fixture `hooks/__tests__/activityRoster.tsx`): `activityGate-7476`, `activityGrant-12081`, `activityType-6730`, and `layout/__tests__/AppHeader.inboxVariant.test.tsx` (its metadata stub lists an app with `hr_contract`; its grant payload grants `hr_contract` where it grants `sys_activity`). One assertion is reversed on purpose. 7476's "no MetadataProvider at all" case asserted an unfiltered read. Under this card's ruling there is no roster, so there is no read.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the 14 feed files (`sharedUserFeeds*`, `sharedInboxFeed*`, `ActivityFeed*`, `AppHeader.inboxVariant`): `Test Files 14 passed (14)`, `Tests 133 passed (133)`, exit 0, on `84b8f5632`.
- The wider set, `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/`, `src/layout/`, `src/console/home/`, `src/views/RecordDetailView*`, `src/views/record-preview/` and `apps/console` `record-block-record-reach`: `Test Files 222 passed (222)`, `Tests 1626 passed (1626)`, exit 0, on `95510b3bf`. That run started before `84b8f5632`, which only destructures the gate callbacks for the memo's dependency list.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsconfig.test.json`), after the `@object-ui/app-shell^...` closure build: exit 0 on `84b8f5632`.
- **Ablation** (via objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which verifies the mutation on disk and restores it). The anchor `$filter: { object_name: { $in: roster } },` was hit 1 time and dropped to 0, and the replacement marker rose from 0 to 1. The new pin went red: `Tests 5 failed | 13 passed (18)`. Restore was proven: blob `c9fb21067517` equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- Pre-tsc battery, all exit 0: `check:phantom-deps`, `self-import`, `unreferenced-sources`, `doc-example-readers`, `handler-key-reads`, `side-effects-array`, `element-data-source-declaration`, `spec-symbols`, `action-forward-parity`, `designer-field-key-parity`, `icon-record-names`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift`, `i18n-designer-parity`, `control-bytes`. Also exit 0: `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:test-path-roots`.
- ESLint, narrowed: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 7 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files.
  - (1) The population is `eslint.config.js`'s `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` minus its `ignores`, and all 7 files are inside it.
  - (2) The JSON output counts 7 files, 0 errors. The warnings are all pre-existing lines of `AppHeader.inboxVariant.test.tsx`. One `exhaustive-deps` warning on the new memo was fixed in `84b8f5632`, and `sharedUserFeeds.ts` now lints clean.
  - (3) Invariance: the config sets no `parserOptions.project`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.
- Not run: `scripts/__tests__/check-hand-rolled-comment-mask.test.ts`. No test here reads source.

## Acceptance notes

- **Browser reading on HotCRM: NOT MEASURED**, reason: this run had no HotCRM backend. It belongs to the landing seat or the maintainer, per the card.
- An admin whose Setup app lists `sys_user` / `sys_organization` / `sys_team` still sees edits to those records. That follows the ruling, which derives the roster from the apps. JWKS keys, data migrations and `knowledge_article` owner backfills drop out unless an app the user opens lists those objects.
- A host with no `MetadataProvider` (a standalone embed of the bell) now shows an empty activity feed instead of an unfiltered one, per the ruling.
- The sign-in exclusion drops any user's sign-in stamp, not only the reader's own. The card's "What happens" names "every login", and an admin otherwise sees one row per user per sign-in.
- File surface: `layout/__tests__/AppHeader.inboxVariant.test.tsx` was edited beyond the claim's list. It pins the bell's activity reading through `AppHeader`, and it went red under the new roster rule (9 cases). Only its metadata stub and one grant payload changed.
